surfaces.part: sawn end with rings (left, vertical oval)

answer.evidence: The log is drawn as a cylinder seen side-on. Row 3 is the outline and row 4 is a single light highlight line (L=180). Rows 5-9 are speckled bark in one tone, and rows 10-12 darken toward the underside (L=60-81), with the dark outline and shadow at rows 13-14. That is ordinary cylinder shading, not a flat horizontal seat plane. There is no band that ends in a front-edge line and eave shadow, and no ellipse on top. The only ellipse-like shape is the sawn end with its rings, which is a vertical face spanning rows 6-12 on the left. The seat surface therefore shows at most a 1-row highlight and reads as front elevation / side profile rather than a seat seen from above.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate has about 5 brown steps on the bark: highlight along the top, mid, shadow underside and a dark brown edge. The sawn end has a lighter ring face with 2-3 ring tones, plus a small green moss/leaf accent. The dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the outline is a tinted dark brown beside the wood, not a black sticker line. Measured facts: 11 visible tones per tile against 9 for the hedge reference, 0% near-flat coverage, and 11 total distinct colours, the same as the hedge. It sits at the density of the bench-wood and hedge references. The bark grain lines and ring detail keep large areas from being flat fills. It is slightly simpler than the well and stall references, but this is a small single-tile-height prop, so that does not count against it. It would sit acceptably next to the references.

answer.evidence: Column scans at x=8, 15 and 23 show a 1-row dark outline at row 3 and a light highlight at row 4. Rows 5-9 are a 5-row speckled bark band (L about 105), which I read as the top surface. Row 10 is a darker line (L=60) that acts as the front-edge line, followed by a 3-row front/underside face at rows 10-12. Rows 13-14 are dark ground shadow. The sawn end with rings is a vertical oval on the left and counts as the log's end face, not a top. The result is borderline: the cylindrical log could also read as a side profile, but the bark band with texture and an edge line gives a modest top plus a front face.

styleAnswer.evidence: The log has about 5 brown steps on the bark: a highlight along the top, mid bark, dark grain streaks and a deep underside. The sawn end shows concentric ring tones, and a small green leaf adds variety. The outline leans dark brown against the wood, and the measured 0% near-neutral dark edge pixels confirms it is tinted, not a black sticker line. Measured facts are 11 visible tones per tile and 0% near-flat coverage. That is at or above the prop-hedge reference (9 tones, 0% flat) and below only the heavily detailed stall and well. The bench and lamp references measure 0 tones per tile because they are thin, so they are no use for density. No large flat fills appear. It is a little simpler than the richest references, but a careful artist would accept it beside the hedge and bench.
